primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Where a person was convicted of an offense that has since been decriminalized, the person may petition the Superior Court and the court shall direct the records to be physically destroyed.
Recorded on the track as authority. The current scope of "decriminalized" after Menditto is unresolved and the case was not read in full.

Recorded on the track as authority. Held that § 54-142d did not compel erasure of a violation of probation finding premised on a later-decriminalized offense. Not read in full; no reporter citation is recorded on the track.

counselFlags.statement: The remedy is physical destruction of all police and court records and records of the state's or prosecuting attorney pertaining to the case — not erasure. It is a stronger outcome and it is separate from the cannabis erasure petition. Rendered output for this track must not describe the relief as erasure.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That participant copy and rendered output for this track say destruction, and that this track is never merged with the § 54-142v erasure petition.
